sentences.text: The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender

Criminal Petition No.11250 Of 2023
O R D E R:

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.') by the petitioner- sole accused seeking to quash the docket order dated 03.11.2023 in Crl.M.P.No.82 of 2023 in S.C.No.246 of 2017 passed by the Special Judge for Expeditious Trial and Disposal of Rape and POCSO Act Cases, Ranga Reddy District at L.B.Nagar, against him.
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner-accused and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondent - State.
Perused the record.
3. The petitioner/sole accused is facing trial for the offence under Section 3 r/w 4 of POCSO Act.
After completion of examination of PWs 1 to 12, the learned Special Judge deemed it appropriate to frame the following charges under Section 376(1) and 417 of IPC against the accused:.

Charge No.1: That you the accused on 17.07.2016 in the house of the victim situated at Flat No.503,
Garden Residency, Maithri Nagar, Gaddiannaram, Dilsukhnagar, Hyderabad committed rape on the victim, aged 16 years, Crl.Petition No.11250 of 2023 who is minor and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 376(1) of IPC and within my cognizance.

Charge No.2: That you the accused cheated the victim girl by saying false promises that you would marry her and participated in sexual intercourse with her on the disguise of marriage and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 417 of IPC and within my cognizance.
4. After framing of the above charges, an application under Section 311 of Cr.P.C was filed by the petitioner/accused to recall PWs 1 to 12 for the purpose of their further cross examination.

Learned Special Judge by order dated 03.11.2023 refused to allow the prayer of the petitioner and declined to recall the witnesses PWs 1 to 12 on the ground that additional charges were framed only on the basis of evidence which is already on record in the case.
5.

Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that since the additional charges were framed,
the petitioner has a right to cross examine the witnesses.

6. Under Section 217 of Cr.P.C, whenever a charge is altered or added after the commencement of the trial, it is mandatory that witnesses shall be recalled, however, the Court can refuse on the Crl.Petition No.11250 of 2023 ground that the petition was filed with the purpose of delaying and appropriate orders can be passed.
7. As seen from the charges, it is alleged that the petitioner had promised the victim girl that he would marry her and participated in sexual intercourse.

The relevant person who can be cross examined about the said allegation would be the victim girl herself since it is a communication in K Vinay vs The State Of Telangana on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131975454/
1 between the accused and victim girl.

sentences.text: 8. Any information passed on by the victim girl to a third person would be hearsay.
In the circumstances, there is no necessity to recall all the witnesses in the case.
However, this Court deems it appropriate to permit cross examination of the victim/PW2 and the Investigation officer/PW10 regarding the statement of victim.

9. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is partly allowed and the learned Special Judge is directed to recall the witnesses i.e. victim/PW2 and Investigating Officer/PW10 for the purpose of cross examination by the petitioner/accused.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
K.SURENDER, J Date: 16.11.2023
